docs.title: Technician Toolkit
docs.text: Quick troubleshooting procedures for IT support. Each procedure follows the same plan: symptom, quick checks, step-by-step fix, and when to escalate.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: Windows stops with a blue screen showing a sad face and a stop code, then restarts.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Write down the stop code (for example CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED) or take a photo of the screen.
  • Did the problem start after an update, a new driver, a new device or a new program?
  • Does it happen once, or again and again?

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Let the PC restart. If it starts normally, save the user's work first.
  2. Unplug new external devices (USB drives, docks) and test again.
  3. Check Windows updates and drivers: install pending updates.
  4. Repair system files: open PowerShell as administrator and run sfc /scannow, then DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.
  5. Test the memory: run "Windows Memory Diagnostic" from the Start menu and restart.
  6. If the PC cannot start, restart three times to open the recovery menu, then choose Safe mode or Uninstall recent updates.
  7. Keep the crash files from C:\Windows\Minidump and attach the stop code to the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• The blue screen happens several times a day: suspect a hardware problem (memory, disk) and escalate.
  • The PC cannot start even in Safe mode: prepare a replacement PC and recover the data.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: A new user, or a user with a new PC, needs their company mailbox in Outlook, or the mailbox stops syncing.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Does the user have a mailbox? Check that the account is created and enabled.
  • Does the webmail work in a browser? If yes, the problem is the Outlook configuration, not the account.
  • Is the Internet connection working?

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Open Outlook, then File, Add account.
  2. Enter the company email address. With a standard setup, Outlook finds the settings alone.
  3. If it asks for the settings, enter the values given by the mail administrator: incoming server, outgoing server, ports and encryption.
  4. Enter the password of the user and check the box to remember it only on a company PC.
  5. Send a test message and ask the user to reply to confirm that sending and receiving work.
  6. If the mailbox does not sync, remove the account and add it again.
  7. Record the configuration in the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• The account exists but the mailbox does not: send the request to the mail administrator.
  • Sending is blocked while receiving works: the account may have been flagged for spam, escalate to security.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The user cannot log in to their Windows session or an application because they forgot their password, or the account is locked.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Is Caps Lock on? Is the keyboard layout correct (ENG or FR)?
  • Does the user see "wrong password" or "account locked"? A locked account unlocks itself after 30 minutes.
  • Can the user log in on another device with the same password? If yes, the problem is the device, not the password.

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Verify the identity of the user before any change: call them back on a known number, or ask their manager to confirm. Never reset a password on a simple email request.
  2. On the domain controller, open PowerShell as administrator.
  3. Reset the password: Set-ADAccountPassword -Identity firstname.lastname -Reset -NewPassword (Read-Host "New password" -AsSecureString)
  4. Force a change at next login: Set-ADUser -Identity firstname.lastname -ChangePasswordAtLogon $true
  5. Unlock the account if needed: Unlock-ADAccount -Identity firstname.lastname
  6. Give the temporary password by phone, never by email.
  7. Ask the user to log in and choose a new password of at least 10 characters.
  8. Record the action in the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• The identity of the caller cannot be verified.
  • The account keeps getting locked: possible attack or a device with an old saved password. Contact the security team.
  • The user is a VIP or an administrator account.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: A user asks for a program they do not have, for example a file compression tool.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Is the software on the company list of approved software?
  • Is a licence needed, and is one available?
  • Who asks for it, and does the manager agree when it costs money?

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Create a ticket of type Request with the software name, the user and the reason.
  2. Check that the software is approved and free of security warnings (official website only).
  3. Install it on the user's PC with an administrator account. Example with the Windows package manager: winget install 7zip.7zip.
  4. Check that the program starts and that the user can do the task they needed (for example open a compressed file).
  5. Document the version installed in the ticket.
  6. Close the ticket after the user confirms.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• The software is not on the approved list: ask the security team and the manager for an approval.
  • The software needs a paid licence: send the request to the person who manages the budget.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The user cannot open websites or online tools. The network icon shows a warning.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Is the user on Wi-Fi or cable? Is the cable plugged in, and is Wi-Fi enabled (no airplane mode)?
  • Do other colleagues have the same problem? If yes, the problem is the network, not the PC.
  • Does an internal site or shared folder still work? If yes, the local network is fine and the problem is the Internet link or DNS.

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Check the IP configuration: ipconfig. An address starting with 169.254 means the PC did not get an address from the DHCP server.
  2. Ping the gateway (the router address shown by ipconfig): ping 192.168.1.254. No reply means the local network is down.
  3. Ping a public IP: ping 8.8.8.8. A reply means the connection to the Internet works.
  4. Ping a name: ping google.com. If the IP works but the name fails, the problem is DNS.
  5. Clear the DNS cache: ipconfig /flushdns.
  6. Renew the address: ipconfig /release, then ipconfig /renew.
  7. Restart the PC, then test again.
  8. Record the results of each ping in the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• Several users are affected: contact the network team or the Internet provider.
  • The gateway does not answer: check the router and the switch.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: A shared printer appears as "Offline" and nobody can print, or print jobs stay in the queue.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Is the printer powered on, with no error light or paper jam?
  • Is the network cable plugged in, or is the printer connected to the Wi-Fi?
  • Can other users print, or only one person? One person means a local problem, everyone means the printer or the print server.

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Find the IP address of the printer (printed configuration page or the printer screen).
  2. Test the network from the user's PC: ping 192.168.1.50 (use the real IP). No reply means a network or power problem.
  3. If the printer replies, restart the print service on the PC: open PowerShell as administrator and run Restart-Service Spooler.
  4. Clear a blocked queue: Stop-Service Spooler, delete the files in C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS, then Start-Service Spooler.
  5. In Settings, Printers and scanners, remove the printer and add it again.
  6. Print a test page and ask the user to confirm.
  7. Record the cause and the fix in the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• The printer does not answer to ping after a power cycle: send a technician on site to check the cable and the printer.
  • Several printers are offline at once: check the print server or the network switch.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: A user deleted a file or a folder by mistake, or an old version of a document was overwritten.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Where was the file: on the PC, in a shared folder on the server, or in cloud storage?
  • When was it deleted? The sooner the better.
  • Did the user empty the Recycle Bin?

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Ask the user to stop saving files in the same folder, so that nothing overwrites the deleted data.
  2. Check the Recycle Bin on the PC: right-click the file, then Restore.
  3. For a file on a shared folder: right-click the folder, Properties, Previous Versions tab, then choose a version from before the deletion.
  4. For cloud storage (OneDrive and similar): open the online Recycle Bin and restore the file.
  5. If nothing is found, restore from the latest backup. Ask the backup administrator and give the exact path and the date.
  6. Open the recovered file with the user to check that it is the right one.
  7. Record what was recovered and where in the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• No backup exists for the file: report it to the manager, so the backup policy can be reviewed.
  • The file is critical or confidential: involve the security team before restoring.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The computer takes a long time to start or to open programs, and applications freeze.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• When did the problem start? After an update, a new program, or for a long time?
  • How long since the last restart? A PC that has been on for weeks needs a restart.
  • Is the problem in one program (for example the browser) or everywhere?

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Restart the PC if it has not been restarted for several days.
  2. Open the Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and sort by CPU, Memory and Disk. Note any program using most of the resources.
  3. Check the free disk space (File Explorer, This PC). Less than 10 % free slows Windows down.
  4. Run the diagnostic script of this toolkit (scripts/windows/diagnostic.ps1) and attach the report to the ticket.
  5. Disable useless startup programs: Task Manager, Startup apps tab.
  6. Install pending Windows updates and restart.
  7. Repair system files: open PowerShell as administrator and run sfc /scannow.
  8. Ask the user to confirm that the speed is back to normal.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• The disk usage stays at 100 % with no obvious program: the disk may be failing, escalate to hardware support.
  • The memory is always full: the PC may need more RAM.
  • The problem comes back after a reinstall: replace the PC.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: A remote user cannot connect to the company VPN. The client shows "authentication failed" or "connection timed out".

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Does the user have Internet at home? Test a public website first.
  • Is the user typing the right login and password (Caps Lock, keyboard layout)?
  • Is the date and time of the PC correct? A wrong clock breaks authentication.

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Ask the user for the exact error message and the time of the attempt.
  2. Check the account in Active Directory: Get-ADUser -Identity firstname.lastname -Properties Enabled, LockedOut. The account must be enabled and not locked.
  3. If the account is locked, run Unlock-ADAccount -Identity firstname.lastname. If the password is the problem, follow the "Forgotten password" procedure.
  4. Check that the user is in the group allowed to use the VPN.
  5. Ask the user to restart the VPN client, then the PC.
  6. Test from another network (for example a phone hotspot): if it works, the home network or router blocks the VPN.
  7. Reinstall the VPN client if the error stays the same.
  8. Record the steps in the ticket and keep the user informed, especially if they have a meeting.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• Several users fail at the same time: the VPN server or the firewall may be down, contact the network team immediately.
  • The account is fine and the client is new, but the error stays: escalate to the VPN administrator.

docs.title: Symptom
docs.text: The computer does not see the Wi-Fi network, or it fails to connect, or it connects without Internet.

docs.title: Quick checks
docs.text:
• Is Wi-Fi enabled, with airplane mode off?
  • Do other devices connect to the same network? If not, the problem is the access point.
  • Is the user close enough to the access point?

docs.title: Step-by-step fix
docs.text:
1. Turn Wi-Fi off and on again from the quick settings.
  2. Check the connection status: netsh wlan show interfaces.
  3. Forget the network (Settings, Network and Internet, Wi-Fi, Manage known networks), then connect again with the password.
  4. Restart the Wi-Fi adapter: Device Manager, Network adapters, right-click the Wi-Fi adapter, Disable then Enable.
  5. Reset the network stack: open PowerShell as administrator and run netsh winsock reset and ipconfig /flushdns, then restart the PC.
  6. Update the Wi-Fi driver from the manufacturer website if the problem continues.
  7. Confirm with the user and record the cause in the ticket.

docs.title: When to escalate
docs.text:
• Nobody can connect to this network: check the access point and the controller.
  • The Wi-Fi adapter is missing in Device Manager: hardware problem.
